messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The test `testBase64EmptyOutputStream()` fails due to misbehavior of the Base64 encoding for empty input arrays. According to the test, encoding an empty byte array `new byte[0]` should produce an empty encoded byte array as well. This is confirmed by the test case calling `testByteByByte(emptyEncoded, emptyDecoded, 76, CRLF)` where `emptyEncoded` and `emptyDecoded` are empty arrays.

From the investigation of `testByteByByte` method in `Base64OutputStreamTest`, we see it tests Base64 encoding and decoding by streaming bytes one by one or in chunks, then comparing the output with the expected encoded and decoded byte arrays.

The culprit lies in the `Base64OutputStream` class, especially the `write`, `close`, and encoding method interplay:
- In `Base64OutputStream.write(byte[], int, int)`, if length is 0 (empty input), the actual Base64 encode is never called because of the condition `if (len > 0)`.
- The encoding is actually finalized and padded during `close()` method of `Base64OutputStream`, where it calls `base64.encode(singleByte, 0, -1);` to indicate EOF to the encoder.
- In the `Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)` method, if `inAvail < 0` indicating EOF, the encoder prepares the final output buffer depending on the current modulus (how many input bytes were buffered).
- Crucially, when EOF is reached, if lineLength > 0, the encoder appends the line separator (CRLF).
- For empty input arrays, no data is fed to the encoder before EOF, but EOF triggers addition of padding and, importantly, the line separator (CRLF). This causes the encoder to output a CRLF sequence even when the input is empty, contrary to the expectation to output an empty array.

Therefore, the root cause is that the Base64 encoder writes out the line separator (CRLF) in the EOF processing path, even when no actual input was encoded. This results in the Base64 encoding of an empty byte array producing a CRLF byte sequence rather than an empty array.

The recent bug reports retrieved are unrelated and do not mention encoding empty input improperly.

This mismatch between expected and actual output is why the test fails.

Fix should focus on the EOF handling in the `Base64.encode` method to avoid writing line separator if no data was received (i.e., length zero input), or the `Base64OutputStream.close()` method's invocation of EOF encoding, ensuring empty input doesn't produce trailing line separators.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
